deep.reconstruction:
CONTEXT. The previous page studies P(φ)=1/M(1,cos φ) as a solution of the second-order ODE y'' = y + 2cot2φ·y' (derivatives in φ). It also uses the Wronskian-type invariant sin2φ·(PQ'−QP') = const, and sets P = ϖ√2/π at φ=45°, where ϖ is the lemniscate constant. The present page derives a quickly convergent AGM-type expression for the derivative P' = dP/dφ, then evaluates it numerically at φ = 45°.

(1) Definitions. Put x = cos φ and P(x) = 1/M(1,x), with the AGM table 1, x; a, b; a', b'; …, where a=(1+x)/2 and b=√x. Since dx/dφ = −sin φ = −√(1−x²), we get P' = dP/dφ = √(1−x²)·M'(x)/M². The page's formula is this derivative with respect to φ (gloss mine).

(2) Derivative of the AGM. Gauss writes dM/dx = M/(2x(1−x²)) · S, where S = 1−x² − 2(a²−b²) − 4(a'²−b'²) − … . Hence
  P' = S / (2x√(1−x²) M(1,x)).
In modern terms put c_0² = 1−x² = k² and c_n² = a_n² − b_n². Then S = c_0² − Σ_{n≥1} 2^n c_n². This is equivalent (my verification) to the classical E/K = 1 − Σ_{n≥0} 2^{n−1} c_n², combined with M(1,k') = π/(2K(k)) and dK/dk = (E − k'²K)/(k k'²). In that form S = (2/K)(E − k'²K).

(3) Recursion for the squares. He computes a² − b² = ((1−x)/2)² = ((1−x²)/4)²/a². This uses 1−x = (1−x²)/(2a)·… and a = (1+x)/2. Similarly a'² − b'² = ¼(a−b)² = (a²−b²)²/(16a'²), and ½(a'²−b'²) = (a²−b²)²/(32a'²). In modern form c_{n+1} = c_n²/(4a_{n+1}).

(4) First normalisation (flawed). He sets c = (1−x²)/8 and c' = cc/a (later cc/aa), and writes P' = 4(c − c' − c'' − …)/(x√(1−x²)M). For x = cos φ this is P' = (8P/sin2φ){c − c' − c'' − …} with c = (1/8)sin²φ.

(5) Corrected normalisation. He then writes c = (1/16)sin²φ, c' = cc/aa, c'' = c'c'/a'a', … . In this scaling c^{(n)} = c_n²/16 exactly. The formula becomes P' = (16P/sin2φ){c − 2c' − 4c'' − 8c''' − …}, which is correct.

(6) Numerical work at φ = 45°.
- AGM of 1 and 0.7071068, with log columns:
  - a1 = 0.8535534, b1 = 0.8408968 (log 9.9247425);
  - a2 = 0.8472251, b2 = 0.8472014;
  - a3 = 0.8472132, log 9.9279927.
- Hence log P = 0.0720073, i.e. P = 1.1803405 = 2K(1/√2)/π = ϖ√2/π.
- The c-column, however, uses the version-(4) data: c = sin²45°/8 = 0.0625.
  - c' = c²/a1² = 0.005361652;
  - c'' = c'²/a2² = 0.000040050;
  - c''' ≈ 0.0000000022 (written 2).
  - Their sum is 0.005401704, so c − Σ = 0.057098296.
- This gives P' = 8P·0.057098296, so log P' = 9.7317205, i.e. P' ≈ 0.539164.

(7) Right-hand column: a difference-quotient check (my interpretation).
- 1.1850926 and 1.1803405 are P(45½°) and P(45°); 1.175678[x] is presumably P(44½°).
- The two P values above differ by 0.0047521. The full difference P(45½°) − P(44½°) = 0.0094146.
- Logs: 7.97380 = log 0.0094146; 4.68557 = −log 206265 (seconds per radian); 3.55630 = log 3600 (1° in seconds).
- So log(ΔP/Δφ_rad) = 9.73193, i.e. P' ≈ 0.53940.

(8) What the true values say. The true value is P'(45°) = 1/K(1/√2) = √2/ϖ = 0.539353 (log 9.731874). Equivalently P·P' = 2/π at 45°, which is the constant 2/π of the previous page. So the difference check (9.73193) lies closer to the truth than the series value (9.73172). The discrepancy exposes the weighting error in step (4).
errors: The formula aa−bb = 1/4 + 1/2·x + 1/4·xx has a sign slip (or misreading): it should be 1/4 − 1/2·x + 1/4·xx = ((1−x)/2)². The following equalities are written correctly.
c' = cc/a (first line) is dimensionally wrong. Gauss himself later writes c' = cc/aa.

The first normalisation c = (1/8)(1−xx) with c^{(n+1)} = (c^{(n)})²/a_{n+1}², combined with unit weights P' = (8P/sin2φ)(c − c' − c'' − …), is wrong beyond the c' term. Its terms equal c0²/8, c1²/4, c2², 16c3², … . The correct terms are c0²/8 − c1²/4 − c2²/2 − c3² − …, i.e. (1/8)(c0² − Σ2^n c_n²). The correct version, c = sin²φ/16 with weights 1, 2, 4, 8, …, is written on the same page.

The numerical evaluation nevertheless used the faulty 1/8 version: c = 0.0625 and c − c' − c'' − c''' = 0.057098296. The c'' term is therefore doubled (4.005e-5 instead of 2.0025e-5). This gives log P' = 9.7317205 (P' = 0.539164) instead of the correct 9.731874 (P' = 0.539353). The relative error is about 3.5e-4.

b1 = √0.7071068 is written 0.8408968; the correct value is 0.8408964. The log 9.9247425 is right, and a2 = 0.8472251 shows the slip was carried forward. The final AGM 0.8472132 is about 1e-7 high (true 0.84721308), with negligible effect on log P (0.0720073 vs 0.0720072).

results.what: Derivative of the AGM: dM(1,x)/dx = M/(2x(1−x²))·[1−x² − 2(a²−b²) − 4(a'²−b'²) − …]. Hence dP/dφ for P = 1/M(1,cos φ) equals (16P/sin2φ)(c − 2c' − 4c'' − …) with c = sin²φ/16 and c^{(n+1)} = (c^{(n)})²/a_{n+1}².
results.modern_name: AGM (Gauss–Salamin/Legendre) series E/K = 1 − Σ 2^{n−1} c_n², equivalently the derivative of the AGM / of K(k)
results.usually_credited_to: Gauss (Determinatio attractionis, 1818, and Nachlass on the AGM); also Legendre's E-formula via Landen transformations

results.what: Recurrence a_n² − b_n² = (a_{n−1}² − b_{n−1}²)²/(16 a_n²), i.e. c_{n+1} = c_n²/(4a_{n+1})

Numerical value of P'(45°) = 1/K(1/√2) = √2/ϖ (equivalently P·P' = 2/π at 45°, the Wronskian/Legendre-relation constant). It is computed by series (with a weighting error) and checked by a central difference quotient over 1°.
results.modern_name: Legendre relation at the singular modulus k = 1/√2; numerical differentiation check

deep.surprise_reason: The AGM-based formula for the derivative of M (equivalently E/K via Σ2^n c_n²) is known Gauss material from the 1799–1818 period. The page is a working computation of it at φ = 45°, interesting mainly for the visible slip in normalisation and the numerical cross-check, not for any new result.

checkable.asserts: At k=k'=1/√2 the bracket S = 1−x² − Σ2^n c_n² equals (2/K)(E − K/2); this compares the numeric value with the AGM sum computed separately
Gauss's series value 8·P·0.057098296 gives log 9.73172, reproducing his log P'
The difference-quotient check gives log P' ≈ 9.73193

transcription_corrections: 'aa−bb = 1/4 + 1/2x + 1/4xx': the middle sign should be minus. The manuscript mark under it may be Gauss's own correction.
'½(a'a'−b'b') = 1/8(a−b)² = 1/8 (aa−bb)²/32a'a'': the value is (aa−bb)²/(32a'a'). The leading '1/8' is probably a superscript '1' numerator.
The German phrase is probably 'P' cos φ; [wenn/ist] das Mittel zwischen 1 u. cos φ ist = 1/P', not 'Prüfst'.
